entities.summary:
Giasone del Maino (1435–1519) was an Italian jurist and one of the last Bartolist commentators on Roman law. He co-authored the treatise 'Tractatus de Successione' with his pupil Filippo Decio.

As a prominent figure in the Italian Renaissance, del Maino's work significantly contributed to the codification of Roman law, influencing the development of modern legal systems. His scholarly achievements earned him recognition as a leading authority in the field of ius civile.

Del Maino's legacy can be seen in the continued relevance of his writings on Roman law, which have shaped the legal landscape of modern nations. His work has been cited by prominent jurists and scholars, ensuring his intellectual contributions remain a cornerstone of legal scholarship.

The meticulous attention to detail in his treatises reflects the high standards of scholarship prevalent during the Italian Renaissance, a testament to the era's commitment to intellectual rigor and pursuit of knowledge.

In the annals of legal history, Giasone del Maino's name stands as a testament to the power of human ingenuity and the indelible mark of scholarship on the fabric of society.
